question: What surveyed elevations does the Cabrillo 15-year report actually publish for its rocky-intertidal monitoring plots, and for each number, was it measured or derived?
headline: 137 surveyed monitoring points across Cabrillo Zones I-III, 126 of them carrying a height in INCHES ABOVE MLLW, measured with a laser leveller and a Trimble receiver in February and March 2004 and published by NPS in 2006. Heights span -4.87 to +91.75 in above MLLW. Nothing here is compared to anything.
not_claimed: No comparison to any DEM, lidar product or hypsometric curve is made or implied.
No floor is set, changed or proposed, and this is not a floor_evidence entry.
The NPS 0.7 ft check is NOT spent. Extracting NPS-published elevations is not spending it; nothing here is compared to it or to anything else.
The GPS standard-deviation column is NOT reconciled with the report's six-centimetre accuracy claim. It is recorded unresolved.
shared/spots.json is not read from or written to by this finding.

source.title: Status and Trends of Ecological Health and Human Use of the Cabrillo National Monument Rocky Intertidal Zone (1990-2005)
source.citation: Becker, Bonnie J. 2006. Status and Trends of Ecological Health and Human Use of the Cabrillo National Monument Rocky Intertidal Zone (1990-2005). Natural Resource Technical Report NPS/PWR/CABR/NRTR--2006/03. National Park Service, Seattle, Washington.
source.publisher: National Park Service, U.S. Department of the Interior, Pacific West Region
source.elevation_appendix: Appendix E: Tidal Height Study by L.A. Victoria, SDSU Special Study, Spring 2004

Table 8.what: List of Zone I monitoring plots

Table 9.what: List of Zone II monitoring plots

Table 10.what: List of Zone III monitoring plots

Appendix E prose.what: method, tide reference, exclusions, GPS statement

Table E-1.what: Tidal heights of CRIMP sites as determined by L.A. Victoria in spring 2004; per-point date, average, standard deviation and individual readings

source.data_use: MARINe asks for acknowledgement only (marine.ucsc.edu/explore-the-data/#data-use). This report is a U.S. National Park Service publication. Cabrillo I is an NPS carve-out site per marinedb.ucsc.edu/marine/data-downloads/nps_navy_sites.csv (CABR / MEDN); nothing was requested from anyone to produce this finding, which reads only the published PDF.

extraction.method: One-time out-of-band extraction with xpdf pdftotext 4.00, then committed as JSON. No parser is added to lidar-recon/probes/, which is standard-library-only, and no dependency is added to the repo.
commands: pdftotext -raw   -f 199 -l 203 cabrillo_report.pdf   # Appendix E prose + Table E-1
pdftotext -table -f 202 -l 203 cabrillo_report.pdf   # Table E-1 by column position
extraction.why_not_layout_mode: pdftotext -layout DESYNCS these tables: it slides the Plot ID column against the rest, so rows are spliced from two or three different plots. The sample row quoted in issue #82 section 5 and repeated in #83 -- 'L3 284 Circular Plot Owl Limpets 32.669396 -117.245625 0.235812 61.47' -- is such a splice and does not exist in the report. It takes the plot id from Table 8's L3 row, the site id and coordinates from L2, the GPS std dev from L3 and the tidal height from L1. The report's actual rows are L1/280/61.47, L2/284/52.22 and L3/283/51.22.
why_raw_and_table_are_trusted: In -raw (content-stream order) each data row is emitted as ONE text run, e.g. 'L1 280 Circular Plot Owl Limpets 32.669477 -117.245499 n/a 61.47'. The row grouping is the PDF's own, not a reconstruction from x/y positions.
-table (which clusters by row) reproduces -raw token for token on all three tables.

The plot-id prefix encodes the target species and the alignment reproduces it exactly: L=Owl Limpets, B=Barnacles, M=Mussels, Pe=rockweed, Po=Goose Barnacles, T=Red Algal Turf, G=Surfgrass, K=Boa Kelp. Under -layout that mapping is scrambled.
Appendix E's Table E-1 is an INDEPENDENT listing of the same heights, keyed by zone/plot/bolt, and every one of the 126 published heights reconciles against it (see verification below).
extraction.table_e1_column_handling: Table E-1 was parsed by column position rather than token order, because which of the three 'Substrate Height' slots is EMPTY is itself evidence -- see report_exclusions. Offsets are measured from the START of the date token: the date column is left aligned and '3/4/2004' and '3/19/2004' differ in length, so anchoring on its end shifts every 19 March row by one character.
extraction.date_format: Table E-1 prints US month/day/year. The order is not assumed: row 27 and rows 107-109 read '3/19/2004', which is only valid month-first. date_recorded is the ISO normalisation; date_recorded_as_published is the string as printed.
extraction.time_of_day: Table E-1 publishes no time of day, so no timezone question arises for the table. The one clock time the report states, '4:20pm' on 8 February 2004, is local with no offset given and is not used as data here.

units.heights_as_published: INCHES above MLLW. This is the report's own unit, stated in the legend of Tables 8, 9 and 10 ('Tidal height measured in inches above MLLW') and in the Table E-1 caption ('All heights are in inches above MLLW').
units.derived_fields: Every field whose name ends in _DERIVED is computed by this extraction and was NOT published. The only derivation performed is inches -> feet at exactly 12 inches = 1 foot, rounded to 4 decimals. Published inch values are carried unrounded alongside.
how_to_tell_measured_from_derived: *_as_published holds the exact string printed in the report, including its ND and n/a sentinels.
height_in_above_mllw, height_std_dev_in, readings_in_above_mllw, latitude_deg, longitude_deg and gps_std_dev.value are the report's numbers, parsed to float, not transformed.
*_DERIVED is this repo's arithmetic on the report's numbers.

readings_in_above_mllw are the individual laser-leveller readings; height_in_above_mllw is the report's own average of them. The average is the report's derivation, not this repo's, and 126 of 130 Appendix E rows reproduce it to within 0.02 in -- see verification.appendix_e_average_check.

datum_and_method.vertical_datum: MLLW, stated by the report in three places: the legends of Tables 8-10, the caption of Table E-1, and Appendix E's calibration formula.
datum_and_method.instrument: Laser leveller on a tripod emitting a beam in 360 degree rotation, with an eight-foot ruler / stadia pole held perpendicular to the plot surface and a detector run along it until it met the beam.
datum_and_method.horizontal: Trimble receiver, more than six satellites, downloaded via Pathfinder software; UTM NAD 1983. The report records that US Navy shapefiles would not line up under State Plane 1927 CA Zone VI and did line up under UTM NAD83, and concludes the Navy maps were labelled with the wrong projection.
datum_and_method.tie_to_datum_verbatim: CALIBRATE: Stillwater Measurement - Low Tide Measurement = Conversion Factor / Plot Measurement - Conversion Factor = Substrate Height
datum_and_method.tie_to_datum_attribution: the report states this formula was 'obtained from UCSC'
datum_and_method.how_the_still_water_line_was_used: Stillwater height was read against the stadia pole at the water's edge at a recorded time, one to three times per session; the published tide height for that time and place then converts every plot reading in that session to a height above MLLW.
datum_and_method.reported_height_uncertainty: 'Standard deviation of the tidal height measurement is approximately 4 inches' -- legend of Tables 8, 9 and 10. Per-session values in Table E-1 are finer grained; see sessions[].
datum_and_method.surveyor_caveat_verbatim: 'This measurement is subject to your belief of where the tide actually is still and topographic features such as pools and slope may confuse your perception.'

tide_reference.why_this_matters: The heights in this finding are referenced to MLLW as realised at NOAA 9410170 (San Diego), NOT at 9410230, which is the station shared/spots.json binds to cabrillo-tidepools. This is provenance carried with the data, not a footnote, and it is the reason the two are not interchangeable without saying so.
tide_reference.report_verbatim_on_station_choice: The low tide measurement was obtained from the NOAA website for verified coastline data. The closest data collection point for actual tidal heights was the San Diego Station (9410170)
tide_reference.report_verbatim_on_the_difference: To be sure that these data were within our accuracy requirements, the predicted tidal heights for this San Diego location and the study area were compared. The difference in measurements for this comparison was less than one inch and fell with the range of accuracy for the study data.
read_carefully: The heights themselves were calibrated against VERIFIED (observed) water levels at 9410170, not predictions.

The 'less than one inch' figure is a comparison of PREDICTED heights between the San Diego station and the study area. It is the report's own justification for using a station about 6 km away; it is not a measured offset between 9410170 and 9410230, and no such comparison is made here.
'fell with the range of accuracy' is verbatim; the report appears to mean 'fell within'.

gps_std_dev_unresolved.what_the_column_is: Tables 8, 9 and 10 carry a column headed 'Std. Dev.', defined in each legend as 'the standard deviation of the GPS measurements'. No unit is stated anywhere in the report.
gps_std_dev_unresolved.the_conflicting_statement: Appendix E states 'Each location was recorded within six centimeters of accuracy. This Trimbel device used more than six satellites to fix the position.'
gps_std_dev_unresolved.why_it_cannot_be_reconciled: If the column were centimetres, the values would be 0.04-0.52 cm, i.e. sub-millimetre GPS, which no 2004 mapping-grade Trimble receiver delivered and which contradicts nothing in the report but is not credible. If it were metres, values up to 0.52 m are eight times the stated six-centimetre accuracy. Both readings conflict with the six-centimetre claim in opposite directions, so the unit cannot be inferred from the number alone, and the report never states it.
gps_std_dev_unresolved.what_is_recorded: gps_std_dev.value carries the number as published, gps_std_dev.unit is null, and gps_std_dev.unit_status is 'unknown_unresolved' on every point. The 'n/a' entries are carried as unit_status with value null; the table legend defines n/a as 'not applicable (measurement is an estimate)'.
gps_std_dev_unresolved.note_on_issue_82: Issue #82 section 5 gives the range as 0.067-0.521. That is Zone I only. Across all three tables the range is 0.044647-0.521161.

report_exclusions.report_verbatim: When the data were analyzed it was determined that the point height for Zone II M2 was not recorded correctly on the original field sheets, this value is omitted from the final data.
report_exclusions.how_it_survives_extraction: Appendix E row 44 (Zone II M2, site 246, 8 February 2004) publishes average 'n/a' and standard deviation 'n/a' while still printing its two raw readings, -24.09 and -20.14. Table 9 prints its tidal height as 'ND'. The point is retained in points[] with height_in_above_mllw null, its raw readings preserved, and flags height_not_determined and zone_ii_m2_height_omitted_by_report.

report_exclusions.report_verbatim: It was also determined that the second substrate height on February 8th at 4:20pm was not accurate and this value was excluded when calculating the average substrate height and the standard deviation.
report_exclusions.how_it_survives_extraction: This is visible structurally, not merely asserted. Table E-1 has three reading slots. On ALL 36 rows dated 8 February 2004 the SECOND slot is empty and the first and third are filled; no row on any other date has that pattern. That is the excluded 16:20 reading. Every affected point carries readings_in_above_mllw with null in position 2 and the flag feb_8_1620_second_reading_excluded.
report_exclusions.why_36_rows_but_35_points: Appendix E row 55 (Zone II L4, 8 February) is one of the 36, but it was superseded by a 19 March re-measurement, so the L4 point joins row 56 instead and does not carry the flag. Row 55 is retained in appendix_e_rows[] with its empty second slot intact.
report_exclusions.verified_by: reading-slot occupancy counted by column position across all 130 Table E-1 rows: 8 Feb 2004 -> 36 rows, all 'X.X'; 4 Mar -> 37 rows all 'XXX'; 7 Feb -> 8 rows 'X..', 25 'XX.', 18 'XXX'; 19 Mar -> 2 rows 'XX.', 4 'XXX'.

other_report_anomalies_carried_through.what: Four Zone II rows publish an average that is not the mean of the readings printed beside it: Appendix E rows 61 (B3, site 256, avg 16.76 vs readings 23.16/27.11, mean 25.135), 62 (B4, site 259, avg 16.92 vs 23.41/27.36, mean 25.385), 64 (PE4, site 258, avg 13.76 vs 18.66/22.61, mean 20.635) and 65 (PE5, site 265, avg 15.59 vs 21.41/25.36, mean 23.385). Row 65's readings are also character-for-character identical to row 46's (M4, site 254), whose own average 23.39 does reconcile.
other_report_anomalies_carried_through.what_is_not_claimed: No attempt is made to decide whether the averages or the readings are wrong. The published averages are what Table 9 carries forward, so they are what height_in_above_mllw holds; the discrepancy is flagged on the point, not silently resolved.

other_report_anomalies_carried_through.what: Four points were measured twice and the published tables use the later measurement. Zone II L4 (site 242): Appendix E row 55, 8 Feb, 30.14 in, labelled 'L4 (est pnt)', superseded by row 56, 19 Mar, 29.98 in. Zone III M2 (site 015): row 121, 7 Feb, 35.51 in, superseded by row 122, 19 Mar, 28.98 in. Zone III K6 C and K6 S (site 004): rows 110 and 111, 7 Feb, 21.75 and 19.50 in, superseded by rows 108 and 109, 19 Mar, 4.23 and 1.23 in.
other_report_anomalies_carried_through.note: Row 121's readings are identical to row 120's (Zone III M1, site 024), which is the most likely reason M2 was re-measured. The superseded rows are retained in appendix_e_rows[] and named in each point's superseded_appendix_e_rows.

other_report_anomalies_carried_through.what: Zone I T2 S and Zone I K6 N are ONE physical point. Table 8 prints identical coordinates (32.669022, -117.245342), identical GPS std dev (0.189513) and identical height (8.22 in) for both, and Appendix E row 25 labels that single row 'Area 1 T2s, K6n'. This is the report's own bookkeeping, not a duplicate introduced by extraction.

Zone III T2's north bolt appears in Appendix E row 93 with its Bolt column reading 'B' rather than 'N', though its site id is 008N and its location label is 'Area 3 T2n'. Table 10 prints it as N with height 31.75 in, which is row 93's average. Joined on that basis and flagged.

Zone II L7 (site 242A) and L8 (site 266A) print latitude 'n/a' and longitude 'ND'. Both still carry heights (48.26 and 70.26 in) from Appendix E rows 59 and 60, which have no site id in the Site ID column at all. They are surveyed heights without published positions.

The report's own prose says 'within each zone are 17 photoplots (Po, Pe, M, B), 6 line transects (T, G, K) and 6 circular owl limpet transects (L)'. Tables 8-10 list 21 photoplots per zone, not 17, and Zone II lists 8 circular limpet plots, not 6. Recorded as an internal inconsistency in the report's description of its own design; the tables are what this finding extracts.

vintage_and_scope.measured: February and March 2004; report published June 2006
vintage_and_scope.programme: CRIMP / NPS Long-Term Monitoring plots at Cabrillo National Monument, measured as an SDSU special study by L.A. Victoria.
vintage_and_scope.not_the_same_as: This is NOT MARINe Coastal Biodiversity Survey topography. Different programme, different plots, different measurement chain. A CBS topography surface for the cabrillo1 site exists separately at marinedb.ucsc.edu/static/biodiversity/cabrillo1-topo.jpg and is not touched here.
vintage_and_scope.physical_caveat: These reefs bury and scour seasonally, so a 2004 substrate height is not a claim about the substrate height today.
vintage_and_scope.zones: Cabrillo Zones I, II and III run north to south along the Point Loma bench. spots.json's cabrillo-tidepools pin (32.669, -117.245) sits inside Zone I.

verification.record_count: 137 surveyed points (Zone I 45, Zone II 47, Zone III 45) and 130 Appendix E rows.
verification.table_to_appendix_e_reconciliation: Every one of the 126 published heights in Tables 8-10 equals the substrate-height average of a Table E-1 row. 125 join on (zone, plot letter, plot number, bolt); the two that do not are Zone I K6 N and Zone III T2 N, both explained above and pinned explicitly rather than fuzzy-matched. The 11 ND heights have no Table E-1 row, as expected. The 6 Table E-1 rows that match no published height are row 44 (Zone II M2, average n/a) and the 5 superseded rows 55, 110, 111, 121 plus row 93, which matches by value under the bolt-letter flag.
verification.appendix_e_average_check: 126 of 130 Table E-1 rows reproduce their published average as the mean of their own listed readings to within 0.02 in. The 4 that do not are rows 61, 62, 64 and 65, flagged above. Row 44 publishes no average.
verification.alignment_check: pdftotext -raw and pdftotext -table agree token for token on Tables 8, 9 and 10, and the plot-id-prefix to target-species mapping is reproduced exactly under both. pdftotext -layout does not agree with either and is not used.
what_was_not_verified: The GPS standard-deviation unit. Unresolved by construction -- see gps_std_dev_unresolved.
Whether any of these points can still be found on the rock, or whether the substrate at them has changed since 2004.
Any relationship between these heights and any DEM, lidar product, MARINe CBS topography surface, or the NPS 0.7 ft figure. None was computed and none is implied.

The report's page images were not rendered; no pdftoppm or equivalent was available. Alignment is established from the PDF content stream instead, which is the stronger evidence for row grouping, but no human eye has seen the typeset page.
